engineering.title: CTE Model Curriculum Standards: Engineering and Architecture

standards.text: Communicate and interpret information clearly in industry-standard visual and written formats.
Explain the classification and use of various components, symbols, abbreviations, and media common to technical drawings.
Describe the current industry standards for illustration and layout.
Draw flat layouts of a variety of objects by using the correct drafting tools, techniques, and media.
Organize and complete an assembly drawing using information collected from detailed drawings.
Create reports and data sheets for writing specifications.
Demonstrate the sketching process used in concept development.
Understand the process of producing proportional two- and three-dimensional sketches and designs.
Apply sketching techniques to a variety of architectural and engineering models.
Present conceptual ideas, analysis, and design concepts using freehand graphic communication techniques.
Identify the fundamentals of the theory, measurement, control, and applications of electrical energy, including alternating and direct currents.

Understand the characteristics of alternating current (AC) and how it is generated; the characteristics of the sine wave; and of AC, tuned, and resonant circuits; and the nature of the frequency spectrum.
Analyze relationships between voltage, current, resistance, and power related to direct current (DC) circuits.
Calculate, construct, measure, and interpret both AC and DC circuits.
Understand how electrical control and protection devices are used in electrical systems.
Calculate loads, currents, and circuit-operating parameters.
Classify and use various electrical components, symbols, abbreviations, media, and standards of electrical drawings.
Analyze, repair, or measure electrical and electronic systems, circuits, or components using appropriate electronic instruments.
Predict the effects of circuit conditions on the basis of measurements and calculations of voltage, current, resistance, and power.
Understand the concepts of physics that are fundamental to engineering technology.
Describe Newton’s laws and how they affect and define the movement of objects.
Explain how the laws of conservation of energy and momentum provide a way to predict and describe the movement of objects.
Compare the effects and applications of heat transfer and thermal dynamic processes.
Explore the fundamentals and properties of waveforms and how waveforms may be used to carry energy.
Analyze how electric and magnetic phenomena are related and know common practical applications.
Understand how the principles of force, work, rate, power, energy, and resistance relate to mechanical, electrical, fluid, and thermal engineering systems.
Differentiate between scalars and vectors.
Solve problems by using the concept of vectoring to predict resultants.
Compare and explore the six simple machines and their applications.
Evaluate how energy is transferred and predict the effects of resistance in mechanical, electrical, fluid, and thermal systems.
Formulate and solve problems by using the appropriate units applied in mechanical, electrical, fluid, and thermal engineering systems.
Employ the design process to solve analysis and design problems.
Understand the steps in the design process.
Determine what information and principles are relevant to a problem and its analysis.
Choose between alternate solutions in solving a problem and be able to justify the choices made in determining a solution.
Translate word problems into mathematical statements when appropriate.
Demonstrate the process of developing multiple details, within design constraints, into a single solution.
Construct a prototype from plans and test it.
Evaluate and redesign a prototype on the basis of collected test data.
Understand industrial engineering processes, including the use of tools and equipment, methods of measurement, and quality assurance.
Know the structure and processes of a quality assurance cycle.
Describe the major manufacturing processes.
Use tools, fasteners, and joining systems employed in selected engineering processes.
Estimate and measure the size of objects in both Standard International and United States units.
Apply appropriate geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T) practices.
Calibrate precision measurement tools and instruments to measure objects.
Understand fundamental control system design and develop systems that complete preprogrammed tasks.
Identify the elements and processes necessary to develop a controlled system that performs a task.
Demonstrate the use of sensors for data collection and process correction in controlled systems.
Perform tests, collect data, analyze relationships, and display data in a simulated or modeled system using appropriate tools and technology.
Program a computing device to control systems or process.
Use motors, solenoids, and similar devices as output mechanisms in controlled systems.
Assemble input, processing, and output devices to create controlled systems capable of accurately completing a preprogrammed task.
Understand the fundamentals of systems and market influences on products as they are developed and released to production.
Understand the process of product development.
Understand decision matrices and the use of graphic tools in illustrating the development of a product and the processes involved.
Design and construct a culminating project effectively using engineering technology.
Use methods and techniques for employing all engineering technology equipment appropriately.
Apply conventional engineering technology processes and procedures accurately, appropriately, and safely.
Apply the concepts of engineering technology to the tools, equipment, projects, and procedures of the Engineering Technology Pathway.
Understand the methods of creating both written and digital portfolios.
Develop a binder or digital portfolio representative of student work for presentation.
Give an effective oral presentation of a portfolio.
Understand historical and current events related to engineering design and their effects on society.
Know historical and current events that have relevance to engineering design.
Interpret the development of graphic language in relation to engineering design.
Understand the effective use of engineering design equipment.
Employ engineering design equipment using the appropriate methods and techniques.
Apply conventional engineering design equipment procedures accurately, appropriately, and safely.
Apply the concepts of engineering design to the tools, equipment, projects, and procedures of the Engineering Design Pathway.
Understand the sketching process used in concept development.
Apply sketching techniques to a variety of architectural models.
Produce proportional two- and three-dimensional sketches and designs.
Present conceptual ideas, analysis, and design concepts using freehand, graphic, communication techniques.
Understand measurement systems as they apply to engineering design.
Know how the various measurement systems are used in engineering drawings.
Understand the degree of accuracy necessary for engineering design.
Use proper projection techniques to develop orthographic drawings.
Understand the concepts and procedures necessary for producing drawings.
Develop multiview drawings using the orthographic projection process.
Understand the various techniques for viewing objects.
Use the concepts of geometric construction in the development of design drawings.
Apply pictorial drawings derived from orthographic multiview drawings and sketches.
Understand the applications and functions of sectional views.
Understand the function of sectional views.
Clarify hidden features of an object using a sectional view and appropriate cutting planes.
Understand the applications and functions of auxiliary views.
Understand the function of auxiliary views.
Use auxiliary views to clarify the true shape and size of an object.
Understand and apply proper dimensioning standards to drawings.
Know a variety of drafting applications and understand the proper dimensioning standards for each.
Apply dimension to various objects and features.
Understand the tolerance relationships between mating parts.
Understand what constitutes mating parts in engineering design.
Interpret geometric tolerancing symbols in a drawing.
Use tolerancing in an engineering drawing.
Understand the methods of applying text to a drawing.
Describe the processes of lettering and/or text editing.
Implement standard methods of title block creation and use.
Develop drawings using notes and specifications.
Plan, prepare, and interpret drawings and models through traditional drafting or computer-aided design (CAD) techniques.
Understand the methods of creating both written and digital portfolios.
Develop a binder or digital portfolio representative of completed work for presentation.
Give an effective oral presentation of a portfolio.

standards.title: Enlightenment and democratic ideas
standards.text: Describe how Enlightenment thought and emerging ideas about democracy shaped the setting for the founding of the United States.
standards.example: Read Locke on consent and an excerpt from the Declaration of Independence. Identify one shared idea about who gives a government its authority.

standards.title: Natural rights and the Bill of Rights
standards.text: Analyze the ideas behind the American Revolution, including the founders’ belief in God-given rights, and the debates over writing and ratifying the Constitution and adding the Bill of Rights.
standards.example: Compare a Federalist and an Anti-Federalist argument about a bill of rights. Use evidence from each to explain why the issue mattered during ratification.

standards.text: Solve linear equations and inequalities with one unknown, including equations with letter coefficients.
standards.example: Solve ax + 4 = 16 for x when a is nonzero.

standards.text: Interpret the graph of a two-variable equation as all ordered pairs that satisfy it.
standards.example: Which of (2, 5) and (3, 5) lies on y = 2x + 1?

standards.text: Solve absolute-value equations and inequalities, graph the solutions, and interpret them in context.
standards.example: A part must be within 0.2 mm of 10 mm. Graph the acceptable lengths.

standards.text: Graph linear inequalities as half-planes and identify where their solution regions overlap.
standards.example: Shade the region satisfying y > x and y ≤ 4. Which boundary is dashed?

standards.text: Interpret a derivative as an instantaneous rate of change and apply it in context.
standards.example: For a cart at position s(t) = 3t² meters, find its velocity at 2 seconds.

standards.text: Explain the chain rule, justify it, and apply it to differentiate composite functions.
Use multiple approaches to begin creative endeavors.
Shape an artistic investigation of an aspect of present day life using a contemporary practice of art or design.
Engage in making a work of art or design without having a preconceived plan.
Explain how traditional and nontraditional materials may impact human health and the environment and demonstrate safe handling of materials, tools, and equipment.
Collaboratively develop a proposal for an installation, artwork, or space design that transforms the perception and experience of a particular place.
Apply relevant criteria from traditional and contemporary cultural contexts to examine, reflect on, and plan revisions for works of art and design in progress.
Analyze, select, and curate artifacts and/or artworks for presentation and preservation.
Analyze and evaluate the reasons and ways an exhibition is presented.
Analyze and describe the impact that an exhibition or collection has on personal awareness of social, cultural, or political beliefs and understandings.
Hypothesize ways in which art influences perception and understanding of human experiences.
Analyze how one’s understanding of the world is affected by experiencing visual imagery.
Interpret an artwork or collection of works, supported by relevant and sufficient evidence found in the work and its various contexts.
Establish relevant criteria in order to evaluate a work of art or collection of works.
Document the process of developing early stage ideas to fully elaborated ideas.
Describe how knowledge of culture, traditions, and history may influence personal responses to art.
